After seeing him die, the knowledge that she could have saved him pushed her over the edge. Some part of her blamed Mathieu for not showing the letter sooner, but she hated herself for it. He was just a child, he didn't deserve her hatred. The letter said that Chatles was somehow surviving on an island in the Chagos, the Peros Banhos Atoll to be exact. This is where she needed to go. It was years ago, but she hoped for any scrap of evidence that would lead her to his executioners.

Anna had hired a boat. She, Lara and her girls would initially use it to scout the atoll. It was too dangerous for them to land, there was too much unknown information about the terrorist group. They could be anywhere, including the Chagos. No, they couldn't conduct a proper search, at least for now. The search mission would have to be by boat. The plan was to scout the atoll to look for any signs of life, any evidence of human interference. Anna looked out onto the ocean. The Peros Banhos Atoll was straight ahead. She was desperate for answers. Previous attempts to find any evidence of who or where the terrorists were had come up empty. This was one of her last leads. They began the search at the South-West corner of the atoll. They followed the coastline up to Ile du Coin. As they passed the former settlement, Anna peered through the coconut trees. She thought she had seen a black shape within the plantation. She heard shouts. It was a strange mixture of broken French and Mauritian Creole. The distinctive revving of a speedboat engine could be heard.

'Lara, we need to get out of here now!'. Lara began to turn the boat around, heading back towards Mauritius. 'Lilith, Lana, get your guns ready, we might need them' Lara ordered. Several figures emerged from the trees, all carrying machine guns. There were about ten of them. They all opened fire on the boat. 'Everyone, get down!'. Anna dropped to the floor. Thankfully, the boat was out of range for their shots to be accurate, however she still heard the occasional 'thunk' of bullets hitting the hull. Eventually it stopped as Lara pulled away from the island. It was several minutes before Anna dared to peek above cover. They were well out of range. Although the site she saw behind her was what scared her. A black speedboat rounded the bottom of the atoll. Despite it being quite a distance away, Anna could see some sort of structured built on the back of it. A man was stood next. She speculated that it must have been some sort of mounted machine gun. The boat prowled the coast, far away enough for Anna to feel relatively safe. It was a close call, but at least they had found the terrorists.

Suddenly, he remembered. The gift! If he presented it to the Queen, he might be rewarded for his efforts! He quickly ran out of the city, and off to the pit he had thrown the creature into. The spider had neglected to care for the creature, only begrudgingly throwing meat into the pit every once in a while. The spider hoisted up young Johbla by the thread he had left near the top of the hole, and began dragging the SeaFairer to the top of Reginapolis.

Once at the top, the four-eyed Fulcrid knocked on the doors to the chamber. There the Queen sat, writing things down on the arm of her throne. The spider threw Johbla against the base of the throne, and began rapidly clicking, "Mother, please excuse me coming in! I brought a gift for you! Can I have ,meat for it please, please?"

The Fuclrid's clicking was ecstatic in nature, and his fangs were covered in his own drool. Once the Queen saw the bundle of webs stir, she became interested in what she was brought. "What is this, my child?", inquired the Queen.

"I dunno, but it was moving and it smelled like salt! I've never, ever seen one of these things, ever! I swear! Which means that it's really valuable, and that I should get a meaty reward! Please mother!".

"Oh, alright.", the Queen said, throwing the young spider her half finished rabbit leg.

"Yay! Thanks!", replied the spider, running away with glee, rabbit's leg in his slobbering jaws.
